streetContent.description:
Ennisclare Drive is a rural residential road in the Rural Nassagaweya area of Milton, sitting well north of the town's built-up grid. This is countryside address territory: low-density, spread out, and framed by open land rather than subdivision streets. The road carries a single detached home in the recent record, which tells you most of what you need to know about its scale. It is not a street you pass through on the way to somewhere else. Milton's urban core, the GO Station, and the highway network all sit a drive away, not a walk. What the street offers is distance from the town and proximity to the rural fabric that surrounds it.

The housing stock on Ennisclare Drive is detached, and the recent record shows a single detached home. There is no published price for the street itself; with so few sales, no typical figure or range can be given, and none is offered here. One active listing sits on the street at present. For broader context, homes across the Rural Nassagaweya area typically trade around $1,550,000, though that is the neighbourhood's figure and not this street's. The street reads as a small rural address rather than a developed residential run.

Daily needs sit at driving distance. Brookville Park is roughly nine minutes away by car, and Moffat Park about fourteen, both serving as the closest green space to the street. Grocery runs mean heading into Milton: FreshCo, Sobeys, and Walmart all sit around twenty-six to twenty-seven minutes out, with Canadian Superstore a little further. Milton District Hospital is about twenty-six minutes by car, and the Milton GO Station roughly twenty-eight, which shapes the commuting pattern for anyone working toward Toronto.

Schools are spread across the surrounding area. Brookville ES is the nearest public elementary option at about eight minutes by car, with W.I. Dick Middle School, Chris Hadfield PS, and Robert Baldwin PS all in the mid-to-high twenties. On the Catholic side, Holy Rosary Catholic ES, St. Peter Catholic ES, and Bishop P.F. Reding Catholic SS sit in the same range. Places of worship follow the same pattern: the Islamic Community Centre of Milton is about twenty-one minutes away, with the Milton Muslim Community Centre a few minutes further. Highway 401 access at Regional Rd 25 is roughly twenty-six minutes by car.

Ennisclare Drive trades rarely. Over the past year the street recorded a single resale, a detached home, and with so few transactions there is no typical price to publish for the street itself. No price range, no per-type figure, and no days-on-market read can be stated with any confidence, and none is offered here. What the record does show is a street of detached houses in Rural Nassagaweya, with one active listing currently on the market. That is the whole of the quantitative picture, and it is thin by any measure.

Suitability for this street is therefore a question of fit rather than of price benchmarking, and the sections that follow carry that discussion. What can be said is that activity here is episodic: a home comes to market, and then the street goes quiet again for an extended period. The single active listing means supply is not a feature of the street in any meaningful sense; there is no queue of inventory to compare against, no pattern of competing offerings, and no basis for reading negotiation behaviour from one transaction. Readers weighing Ennisclare Drive against other Milton addresses should treat the street's own record as effectively silent on price and lean instead on the wider neighbourhood context set out below.

Across Rural Nassagaweya, detached homes comparable to those on Ennisclare Drive have sold at broadly comparable levels over the past year, and the sample behind that read is large enough to stand on its own. The typical sold price for detached homes in Rural Nassagaweya sits around $1.55M. That figure belongs to the neighbourhood, not to Ennisclare Drive, which has no published price of its own. Homes in this cohort have been taking time to clear, with days on market running well beyond what a busier Milton pocket would show, and the sold-to-ask relationship points to meaningful negotiation room rather than buyers paying at or near asking. Taken together, the neighbourhood picture is one of a slower, more deliberate market where asking prices and final sale prices diverge, and where the pool of comparable detached sales is deep enough to give the read some weight even though the street itself offers almost nothing to work with.

Ennisclare Drive sits in Rural Nassagaweya, a position that makes the car the realistic mode for most trips and the GO train the sensible route into Toronto. The Milton GO Station is a twenty-eight minute drive, and from there the run downtown takes about eighty-eight minutes door to door. For points west and south, the arithmetic is friendlier: Mississauga is twenty-two minutes by car, Burlington twenty, Oakville twenty-four. Pearson is thirty-two minutes, which keeps airport runs within a single sitting. The Highway 401 onramp at Regional Road 25 is twenty-six minutes away, so the 401 is reached without threading through Milton's core. This is a street where the drive is part of the day's shape, not an afterthought.

Brookville ES is the closest public elementary, eight minutes by car, and the nearest of the Halton District School Board options. The other public elementaries, W.I. Dick Middle School, Chris Hadfield PS and Robert Baldwin PS, sit twenty-six to twenty-seven minutes out. On the Catholic side, Holy Rosary Catholic ES is twenty-six minutes and St. Peter Catholic ES twenty-eight, both under the Halton Catholic District School Board. Bishop P.F. Reding Catholic SS is the nearest secondary named here, twenty-eight minutes away. School assignment should be confirmed with the boards directly.
